Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the Pakistani players. The duo of Tanzid Hasan and Mohammad Naim are set to open the innings for Bangladesh. Salman Mirza to start proceedings with the ball. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Now the chase is not going to be easy by any means as the ball has started to hold in the wicket a bit and Pakistan have got the runs on the board. But there will be dew in the second innings, which might aid the Bangladesh batters. Do join us for the chase, which is coming up right away.

For Bangladesh, Nasum Ahmed was clearly the pick of the bowlers, as he finished with 4-0-22-2. He was the only bowler who had an economy rate under six in the entire bowling lineup. Mohammad Saifuddin also bowled until his last over, which went for 19 runs and Taskin Ahmed picked up a couple of wickets in the final over to finish with 3 wickets to his name.

To start with, Pakistan got off to a flying start, as the opening duo of Sahibzada Farhan and Saim Ayub put on 82 for the 1st wicket. At that point, it seemed like 200 was well within reach. However, the wicket did start to get slower as the innings progressed, and shot-making became a bit difficult. Also, after the fall of the first wicket, Bangladesh kept on finding wickets at regular intervals. Sahibzada eventually finished with a well-compiled 63. Hasan Nawaz and Mohammad Nawaz played superb cameos to propel the score close to the 180 mark.

Pakistan finish with 178 big runs on the board. They will be mighty pleased with the total. However, the wicket today was slightly better than what we have seen in the first two games, but nevertheless, 178 is a big total at this venue on any given day.

Just a single to end and only 5 runs come off the final over! Hard length on off, Afridi has another swipe across the line but gets an inside edge and the ball rolls wide of short fine leg. The baters jog across for a single and Pakistan finish with 178/7 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! Well, well! A stark contrast from the previous couple of games for Pakistan and it is just one man - Sahibzada Farhan, who has made all the difference. He has made a tough track look like a regulation T20 pitch but in the last couple of overs, Frhan has found himself off strike and Bangladesh have been able to stem the flow of runs to an extent. With 10 overs to go, Pakistan should be targeting somewhere around 160 and with 9 wickets in hand, they should get it as well. However, if Bangladesh pick up a couple of quick wickets, it could result in a collapse given the nature of this track.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the Bangladesh players, who form a huddle before striding onto the field of play. It will be Sahibzada Farhan to open the innings for Pakistan alongside Saim Ayub. Mahedi Hasan, the off-spinner, will take the new ball. Let's play...

Salman Agha, the Pakistan skipper, says that for them, playing every game the way they want is important right now, more than the results. Adds that they haven't batted well as a team and they have sat down and discussed about it. Informs that they have a couple of changes with Sahibzada Farhan coming in for Fakhar Zaman, who is resting and Khushdil Shah is not playing. Hussain Talat comes in for him.

Bangladesh skipper Litton Das says they will bowl first. On asked about the context of this game, he says it’s important to carry the winning momentum and being an international game, they need to play their best. On what are the areas of improvement, he says they are a good fielding side and he feels this is an area where they want to get relatively better. He mentions that in the last two games, particularly in the second innings of the last 10 overs, there was dew, making batting easier. He says they have made five changes.

PITCH REPORT - Former Pakistani opener Ramiz Raja is inspecting the deck. He starts by saying that generally, in T20 cricket, pitches bring you plenty of runs, but the difficulty is different on this deck. Reckons that there is some steaminess coming off the deck and batting first will be a challenge. For the bowlers, using the cutters will be helpful and the batters will have to find more angles to score and rotation of strike will be key. Also adds that there's been plenty of overnight rain, which means the outfield will be a bit soggy.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Sahibzada Farhan (In for Fakhar Zaman), Saim Ayub, Mohammad Haris (WK), Salman Agha (C), Hasan Nawaz, Hussain Talat (In for Khushdil Shah), Mohammad Nawaz, Faheem Ashraf, Abbas Afridi, Ahmed Daniyal, Salman Mirza.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das (C/WK), Tanzid Hasan (In for Parvez Hossain Emon), Mohammad Naim, Mehidy Hasan Miraz (In for Tawhid Hridoy), Jaker Ali, Shamim Hossain, Mohammad Saifuddin (In for Mustafizur Rahman), Mahedi Hasan, Taskin Ahmed (In for Tanzim Hasan Sakib), Shoriful Islam, Nasum Ahmed (In for Rishad Hossain).
TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

Bangladesh, on the other hand, led by Litton Das, has now won two series on the trot, firstly against Sri Lanka and now against Pakistan. So they are flying high on confidence. In the first game, it was the top order that chased down the Pakistan total in a canter. On the other hand, in the 2nd game, their top order failed, and then we saw the middle and lower order standing tall. Their bowlers, too, have enjoyed bowling on the bowler-friendly Dhaka wicket, wherein their bowlers have delivered as a unit, contributing in different stages of the game. Stay tuned as the toss and team sheets are up next.

It has been a low-scoring series, and Pakistan batters in particular have struggled from the get-go. If in the 1st game they were bowled out for a mere 110-run total, then in the 2nd game they failed to chase down 134, as they got bowled out for 125. The Pakistani top six has failed to get going in both the games, as, except for Fakhar Zaman, none of their top six have managed to cross the double-digit mark in any of the games. The bowling unit as a whole has been fairly decent, and it will be interesting to see if Pakistan will make any wholesale changes going into this game.

Hello and welcome to the third and final game of the three-match T20I series between Bangladesh and Pakistan. The hosts have already won the series, having won the 1st and 2nd games. However, both teams will have a lot to play for. On one side, Bangladesh would target a historic whitewash, whereas on the other hand, Pakistan will look to end the series on a high note.
... MATCH DAY ...

The final act of the T20I series between Bangladesh and Pakistan is upon us at the Shere Bangla National Stadium in Mirpur. With victories in the first two games, Bangladesh have already sealed the series, their first multi-game T20I series win over Pakistan. The hosts will now look to pile on the misery and complete a whitewash, while Salman Agha and his men will be desperate to salvage some pride and head into their Caribbean tour with a bit of momentum. It was the batting that let the visitors down in the second game, as they slumped to 15/5 early on and then 47/7 in their chase of 134. Faheem Ashraf did give Pakistan a glimmer of hope, but they eventually fell short. For the second game in a row, run-outs and soft dismissals plagued their batting effort, leaving little in the way of positives. The onus will now be on the likes of Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Mohammad Haris, and Salman Agha to step up and finish the series on a high. With the ball, however, the visitors have found a few bright spots. Salman Mirza and Ahmed Daniyal have both impressed and will be eager to carry that form into the final clash. Bangladesh, on the other hand, seem to be finding their feet in the format, having now followed up a series win over Sri Lanka with this triumph against Pakistan. It has been their bowling unit that has laid the foundation for success. Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, and Mahedi Hasan have all contributed effectively as a unit. While Litton Das has struggled for runs, Parvez Hossain Emon and Jaker Ali have stepped up with handy contributions on tricky surfaces. Last year, Bangladesh created history by whitewashing Pakistan in their own backyard in Tests and now, they have a chance to repeat the feat in T20Is. Can they get the job done? We shall soon find out.
